answer: Each agent mints an ember at signup: a short-lived proof-of-work token that expires unless refreshed by real compute each epoch. The ember is woven into a thread, an append-only chain that grows only when peers verify the previous links. One violet slot per identity caps extraction per round. Because embers expire fast, an attacker running many clones must keep every ember alive; the single violet slot means each clone extracts little, making swarms unprofitable as thread length grows.
